name: Hallord
summary: The oldest of the Sunken Halls and the arbiter of deep-folk clans. Carved into the Stone Crown's root before the Concord, Hallord has never fallen, never opened its lowest door, and never — in 4,000 years — written down a law. All law is spoken, remembered, and sworn on the First Forge.
role: eldest hold; arbitrator of the clans

ruler.title: Hall-Voice
ruler.note: Named for the nine iron rings of his beard: clan, craft, age, oath, grief, war, craft again (a second mastery), silence, and one ring no one asks about.

districts.name: The First Forge
districts.description: The hall's heart: a forge said to be lit from Orbren's own hammer-fall at the Deep-Forging. Its fire has never gone out. All clan law is sworn here, and steel signed here is trusted continent-wide.

districts.name: The Speaking Stairs
districts.description: A spiral descent where disputes are heard: accuser above, accused below, and the Hall-Voice on the middle step. Verdicts travel up as echoes.

districts.name: The Ring-Vault
districts.description: Where the clans' oath-rings are stored when their bearers die. Generations of iron, each ring a life. The vault's lock has no key; it opens only to a unanimous clan council.

districts.name: The Lowest Door
districts.description: At the hall's deepest point: a door of stone not mined but grown shut, sealed by Khord's first Door-Keepers. No record says what it holds. Every Hall-Voice inherits the duty of not asking.

landmarks.name: The Ring Gallery
landmarks.description: A corridor of ten thousand iron rings, each from a dead deep-folk bearer. Visitors walk it in silence; the deep-folk walk it speaking the names.

landmarks.name: The Surface Porch
landmarks.description: Hallord's only above-ground structure: a stone porch and trade-house where surface folk wait. Deals are struck here because outsiders may pass one threshold only.

landmarks.name: The Humming Shaft
landmarks.description: A mine shaft sealed three years ago by the Deep-Shapers after it began 'ringing' — the same note the Storm-Bound hear at sea. The seal is fresh. The ringing has not stopped.

conflicts: The Humming Shaft: the Deep-Shapers sealed it without consulting the clans, and Hall-Voice Borin has not demanded an answer — which frightens the elders more than the shaft does.
Surface trade is booming and purists resent the Surface Porch's wealth of strange coin.
Greenwood roots breach the lower galleries each spring; the ancient tension with the greenfolk turns litigious.
Young deep-folk take surface contracts and return with dangerous questions about the Lowest Door.

inhabitants.note: ~8,000 souls across nine clan-holds within the greater Hallord system.
Trade factors confined to the Surface Porch; a few stone-wardens' families granted residence.
Verdant kin envoys come each spring to negotiate the root-treaties. They are fed well and watched closely.
A single caravan factor holds the southern trade charter; she has learned never to hum while underground.
